title: Operational Procurement-to-Revenue Handoff Playbook
author: Maya Rodriguez
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the operational workflow, controls, and checklists for progressing a purchase or customer contract from procurement/contract signature through billing and revenue recognition (RevRec). It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, sales operations, and engineering program managers who participate in customer onboarding, vendor procurement, or contract amendments that impact invoicing or revenue timing.

Scope:
- Applies to: customer contracts, marketplace channel agreements, and capitalized procurement where invoicing or revenue recognition is impacted (Hosted API credits, Dedicated/Private Reserved capacity deals, platform add-ons).
- Excludes: one-off expense purchases < $5k (see Procurement Low-Value Flow).

Why this matters:
- Misaligned contract and procurement handoffs are the largest single source of billing delays and RevRec misstatements. Clear checklists and GL mappings prevent missed milestones, incorrect billing cadence, and audit friction.

Key definitions (quick reference):
- Billable Event: a contract-trigger (activation, delivery milestone, committed capacity start) that creates an invoice obligation.
- Revenue Trigger: the specific condition that permits recognizing revenue (often delivery, customer acceptance, or right-to-invoice).
- Deferred Revenue: amounts invoiced or paid where revenue recognition is deferred due to unmet performance obligations.

Ownership and escalation:
1. Contract owner / AE (Sales): ensures signed SOW/Order Form with commercial terms and activation dates entered into Salesforce and attaches executed document to the opportunity.
2. Legal: validates required contract clauses (data residency, escrow, KMS, indemnities).
3. Procurement (vendor side) / Sales Ops (customer side): creates procurement ticket and routes to Finance for billing configuration.
4. Finance (Billing & RevRec): configures billing schedule, GL mappings, and RevRec treatment.
5. Engineering Program Manager (for Dedicated/Private): validates deployment readiness and capacity start date.

Procurement and Contract Checklist (pre-billing):
- Contract metadata captured in Salesforce: billing entity, legal entity, currency, payment terms, taxation flags, SOW attachment.
- Payment terms: Net 30 / Net 45 / prepay; record expected invoice cadence.
- Billing cadence: monthly in arrears, monthly in advance, annual upfront — specify in opportunity.
- Activation trigger: automatic on provisioning / manual on customer acceptance — record explicit wording.
- Pricing components: recurring subscription, usage (tokens/embedding units), overage rates, discounts, credits.
- SLA credits and penalty clauses: route to Finance for contra-revenue treatment guidance.
- Data residency and export restrictions: label contract confidentiality if required.
- Revenue accounting flags: deferred revenue allowed? Capitalizable costs? (Finance to advise).

Operational flow (step-by-step):
1. Signed contract uploaded (Sales): attach executed PDF to opportunity in Salesforce and set Opportunity Stage = "Contracted - Billing Ready".
2. Legal sign-off complete (Legal): update "contract_review" field and set confirmation in the opportunity comments.
3. Sales Ops creates Billing Configure ticket in Zendesk (Billing queue) with the following payload:
   - Opportunity ID, Executed Contract URL, Billing entity, Currency, Payment terms, Invoice recipient, Tax exemption docs, Expected start date, Pricing schedule CSV.
4. Finance Billing reviews within 2 business days and responds with:
   - Required missing items (if any) or "Billing Ready" and assigned Invoice Template.
5. Technical activation check (Engineering): confirm "Capacity Start Date" or "Service Live Date" in the ticket.
6. Invoice creation: First invoice generated according to cadence; if annual upfront, ensure RevRec journal setup in RevRec system (NetSuite/Zuora).
7. RevRec classification: Finance marks revenue as Recognize Now / Deferred with journal entry template included in ticket.
8. Post-invoice validation: Sales Ops confirms customer acceptance and verifies invoice arrived.

Revenue Recognition Rules (summary):
- Recurring hosted API revenue: recognized over service period (time-based), unless the contract has usage-based provable completion events.
- Dedicated reserved capacity: recognized monthly when dedicated capacity is delivered and available to customer; if deployment delayed >14 days, defer revenue until capacity window open.
- One-time setup professional services: recognized on customer acceptance sign-off or when deliverables transferred, per SOW.
- Credits and refunds: recorded as contra-revenue; material credits must be escalated to Finance Manager for approval.

Table: Billing triggers and RevRec action (ASCII table)
| Contract Type                | Bill Trigger                      | RevRec Treatment               | Owner        | SLA 
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------|--------------|-----
| Hosted API subscription     | Start date or provisioning        | Recognize monthly over period | Finance      | 2d  
| Dedicated Reserved Capacity | Customer capacity start timestamp | Recognize when available      | Eng + Finance| 3d  
| Annual prepaid contracts    | Invoice on day 0                  | Defer, recognize monthly      | Finance      | 5d  
| Professional services       | Customer acceptance sign-off      | Recognize on acceptance       | PM / Finance | 7d  

Thresholds and approval matrix (procurement side):
- Purchase Value < $5k: low-value procurement flow (no contract required). Buyer records PO in Coupa and tags finance for FY overhead allocation.
- $5k – $50k: requires Procurement review and Finance notification; one procurement approver + line manager.
- $50k – $250k: requires Procurement lead, Finance & Legal review.
- > $250k: requires VP Finance approval and Legal executive sign-off.

Clause checklist for Legal (to be confirmed before Billing Ready):
- Customer billing entity and tax ID present
- Invoicing address and electronic invoicing consent
- Payment terms explicitly stated
- Termination and refund language (impact on deferred revenue)
- Escrow/KMS/data residency clauses if flagged
- Confidentiality / data processing addendum attached if needed

Templates and examples (snippets):
- Example Billing Configure ticket body (CSV-friendly):
  {
    "opportunity_id": "O-12345",
    "executed_contract_url": "https://redwood.atlassian.net/...",
    "billing_entity": "Redwood, Inc.",
    "currency": "USD",
    "payment_terms": "Net 30",
    "invoice_recipient": "finance-billing@example.com",
    "expected_start_date": "2027-02-01",
    "pricing_schedule": "monthly:4999;usage:per_token:0.0006"
  }

- RevRec journal template (example narration):
  Debit: Deferred Revenue (liability)
  Credit: Revenue - Hosting (income)
  Narration: "Release of deferred annual hosting for Acme Corp. — Feb 2027"

Monitoring and controls:
- Finance runs a monthly Revenue Trigger audit: sample 10% of recently contracted deals and confirm ticket-to-invoice-to-RevRec mapping. Exceptions reported as tickets to finance-ops and legal.
- Billing SLA: Billing Configure tickets should be actioned within 2 business days; exceptions are tracked in the monthly ops dashboard.
- Quarterly spot-check: Legal & Finance to sample high-risk clauses (KMS, escrow, data residency) and ensure special handling is applied (restricted invoice routing, separate legal entity billing).

Common failure modes and remediation:
- Missing invoice recipient / tax docs: remediation = Sales Ops pause provisioning and open ticket to collect docs; Finance to delay invoice until resolved.
- Activation date mismatch: remediation = engineering confirms logs and issues playbook checklist; Finance adjusts first invoice and posts correction entry if necessary.
- SLA credit disputes: apply contra-revenue entry and require credit memo; if material (>5% of contract value) escalate to VP Finance.

Appendix A — GL mapping quick-reference (example):
- Hosted subscription revenue -> GL 4100
- Usage revenue (tokens/units) -> GL 4120
- Professional services revenue -> GL 4300
- Deferred revenue (liability) -> GL 2200
- Credits / refunds -> GL 4900

Appendix B — Contacts and ownership
- Billing & RevRec (Finance): billing-team@redwood.example.com
- Legal Contracts: contracts@redwood.example.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.example.com
- Engineering Activation Leads: eng-activation@redwood.example.com
